content:
Class 5 data handling brings double-bar graphs, pie charts and the mean-median-mode trio — read-carefully marks with a statistics flavour. Here is what the IMO Class 5 data handling chapter tests, with a free 10-question test with charts.

What the Class 5 Maths Olympiad Data Handling chapter tests

  • Bar and double-bar graphs
  • Pie charts as fractions of a whole
  • Mean, median and mode
  • Pictographs, tally and interpretation

Key facts your child should know

  • Mean = sum ÷ count; median = middle after ordering; mode = most frequent.
  • A pie sector worth 1/4 of the circle is 1/4 of the total.
  • Missing value from a mean: sum = mean × count.
  • Always read the scale or key first.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Forgetting to ORDER the data before taking the median.
  • Reading a double-bar pair against the wrong series.
  • Averaging without counting all the values.

Take the free Data Handling test (IMO Class 5)

The 10-question quiz below is drawn from our verified IMO Class 5 question bank. Read each question, pick an answer, then check your score for instant explanations. Want more? The Data Handling Chapter Worksheets e-book has 100 MCQs in 10 worksheets, colourful diagrams with the questions, and full solutions — the ideal Maths Olympiad for Class 5 worksheets PDF with answers.

questions.q: The number of story books read by seven children: 2, 3, 3, 5, 3, 2, 7. What is the mode of this data?
questions.explanation: 3 appears 3 times, more often than any other value, so the mode is 3.

questions.q: A pie chart shows which enclosure 90 zoo visitors liked best. The sector for the lion enclosure takes exactly half of the pie. How many visitors does that sector stand for?
questions.explanation: Half of the whole means half of 90: 90 ÷ 2 = 45 visitors.

questions.explanation: Sorted: 18, 21, 27, 30, 34, 40, 45. There are 7 values, so the median is the 4th value: 30.

questions.q: A double bar graph shows library books borrowed by Grade 5 and Grade 6 over four weeks: Week 1 (Grade 5 24, Grade 6 20); Week 2 (Grade 5 30, Grade 6 26); Week 3 (Grade 5 18, Grade 6 25); Week 4 (Grade 5 28, Grade 6 31). Taking all categories together, which series has the higher total, and by how much?
questions.explanation: Total Grade 5 = 100 and total Grade 6 = 102, so Grade 6 is ahead by 102 − 100 = 2.

questions.q: A pie chart sorts the 240 books in a mobile library: 1/2 of the pie is for fiction and 1/6 is for comics. How many more books does the fiction sector represent than the comics sector?
questions.explanation: fiction = 1/2 of 240 = 120 and comics = 1/6 of 240 = 40; the difference is 120 − 40 = 80 books.
questions.figure: <svg class="qfig" viewBox="0 0 90 108" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img"><circle cx="45" cy="45" r="38" fill="#fff" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="2"/><path d="M45 45 L45.0 7.0 A38 38 0 0 1 45.0 83.0 Z" fill="#db2777" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.6" opacity="0.85"/><path d="M45 45 L45.0 83.0 A38 38 0 0 1 45.0 7.0 Z" fill="#fff" stroke="#334155" stroke-width="1.6" opacity="1"/><text x="45" y="98" font-size="13" text-anchor="middle" fill="#334155" font-weight="700">1/2 of the pie</text></svg>

questions.q: A pie chart sorts 60 cars in a parking lot by colour; 30 of them are white. What fraction of the pie does the sector for white cars take?
questions.explanation: The fraction is 30 out of 60 = 30/60, which simplifies to 1/2.

questions.q: Four students have an average score of 50. 3 of them are 46, 58, 41. What did the fourth student score?
questions.explanation: The 4 values must add to 50 × 4 = 200. The known ones add to 145, so the missing value is 200 − 145 = 55.
questions.figure: <svg class="qfig" viewBox="0 0 198 54" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" role="img"><rect x="8" y="8" width="56" height="30" rx="15" fill="#dbeafe" stroke="#2563eb" stroke-width="1.6"/><text x="36" y="28" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="#334155" font-weight="700">46</text><rect x="70" y="8" width="56" height="30" rx="15" fill="#dcfce7" stroke="#16a34a" stroke-width="1.6"/><text x="98" y="28" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="#334155" font-weight="700">58</text><rect x="132" y="8" width="56" height="30" rx="15" fill="#fce7f3" stroke="#db2777" stroke-width="1.6"/><text x="160" y="28" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="#334155" font-weight="700">41</text></svg>

faq.a: Order them (11, 16, 19, 23, 30) — the middle value is 19.

faq.q: How do you find a missing value when the mean is given?
faq.a: Multiply the mean by the count to get the total, then subtract the known values.
